title: Phantom Thief Jeanne
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Sixteen-year-old Maron Kusakabe lives alone after her parents separated and moved abroad, hiding her loneliness behind a cheerful front. She is the reincarnation of Joan of Arc, and a minor angel named Finn helps her transform into Phantom Thief Jeanne to steal paintings in which a demon lord has hidden demons that steal human hearts from God. Her best friend Miyako, a detective's daughter, hunts Jeanne, while a rival thief, Sinbad, and a flirtatious new neighbor, Chiaki, complicate her life.
life_message: Even a lonely, wounded person can be loved and can give love, and hearts are worth protecting from despair.

content.note: Magical-girl battles sealing demons; MangaDex adds a Gore tag (single source, to verify).
Demons who devour human hearts; betrayal and loneliness themes (ANN; AniList Demons, MU Betrayal).

Maron lives alone, abandoned by separated parents, and struggles to trust (ANN; MU Absent Parent/s, Loneliness).
Teen heroine steals art and evades police, framed as a holy mission.

folkways.japan: Western religious imagery (God, angels, Joan of Arc) is used as fantasy decoration, common in Japanese shoujo, rather than as doctrine.

delivery.evidence: ANN review praises the emotional core of Maron's need to feel wanted; no comment on preachiness.

winners_losers: Maron and the side of God and love are favored; the demon lord's attempt to steal hearts is opposed.
